page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 20 vCPUs. These vCPUs are configured as 20 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.8 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a split performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all landing in the middle 50%. Memory read bandwidth is average at 42.72 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker, falling into the bottom 25% at 21.6 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the contrast between weak single-core and average multi-core metrics, this server is suited for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and software compilation. It is less suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM text generation, where text generation for a 7B model registers in the bottom 10%.
